claim: Genetic ablation or pharmacological inhibition of TRPM3 alleviates inflammatory heat hyperalgesia.
source: Genetic ablation or pharmacological inhibition of the heat-activated cation channel TRPM3 alleviates inflammatory heat hyperalgesia, but the underlying mechanisms are unknown.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work, as indicated by the statement that the mechanisms are unknown, implying established findings about TRPM3's role.

claim: Increased Trpm3 mRNA levels were detected in dorsal root ganglion neurons innervating the inflamed paw.
source: We detected increased Trpm3 mRNA levels in dorsal root ganglion neurons innervating the inflamed paw, and augmented TRP channel-mediated calcium responses, both in the cell bodies and the intact peripheral endings of nociceptors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAscope analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: Augmented TRP channel-mediated calcium responses were observed in both the cell bodies and the intact peripheral endings of nociceptors.
source: We detected increased Trpm3 mRNA levels in dorsal root ganglion neurons innervating the inflamed paw, and augmented TRP channel-mediated calcium responses, both in the cell bodies and the intact peripheral endings of nociceptors.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: Inflammation provoked a pronounced increase in nociceptors with functional co-expression of TRPM3, TRPV1 and TRPA1.
source: In particular, inflammation provoked a pronounced increase in nociceptors with functional co-expression of TRPM3, TRPV1 and TRPA1.
evidence: This claim is supported by functional calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4 and Figure 4F.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of TRPM3 dampened TRPV1- and TRPA1-mediated responses in nociceptors innervating the inflamed paw, but not in those innervating healthy tissue.
source: Finally, pharmacological inhibition of TRPM3 dampened TRPV1- and TRPA1-mediated responses in nociceptors innervating the inflamed paw, but not in those innervating healthy tissue.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using isosakuranetin shown in Figures 2E, 2F, and 4C-E.

claim: Nociceptors detect painful stimuli in peripheral tissues and transmit them as action potentials towards the central nervous system to elicit pain sensation.
source: Painful stimuli are detected by nociceptors in peripheral tissues and are transmitted as action potentials towards the central nervous system to elicit pain sensation (Viana et al., 2019; von Hehn et al., 2012; Vriens et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Under pathological conditions such as inflammation or tissue injury, nociceptors become sensitized to mechanical and thermal stimuli.
source: Under pathological conditions, such as inflammation or tissue injury, nociceptors become sensitized to mechanical and thermal stimuli.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Nociceptor hypersensitivity gives rise to allodynia, hyperalgesia, or spontaneous pain.
source: Such nociceptor hypersensitivity gives rise to allodynia (the sensation of pain to a stimulus that is usually not painful), hyperalgesia (increased pain sensation to a stimulus that is usually painful) or to spontaneous pain without any clear stimulus (Viana et al., 2019; von Hehn et al., 2012; Jensen and Finnerup, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Current analgesic drug therapies are often limited in efficacy in a large number of pain patients and may have severe adverse effects.
source: The current analgesic drug therapies, including non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, opioids, gabapentinoids, and antidepressants, are often limited in efficacy in a large number of pain patients and may have severe adverse effects that limit their use (Colloca et al., 2017; Skolnick, 2018; Voets et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature discussing limitations of current analgesics.

claim: The need for better and safer analgesic drugs is illustrated by the dramatic rise in opioid addiction and related deaths.
source: The need for better and safer analgesic drugs is painfully illustrated by the dramatic rise in opioid addiction and related deaths, known as the opioid crisis (Skolnick, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to literature on the opioid crisis.

claim: Several members of the TRP superfamily of cation channels play key roles as primary molecular sensors in nociceptor neurons.
source: In this context, several members of the transient receptor potential (TRP) superfamily of cation channels play key roles as primary molecular sensors in nociceptor neurons, directly involved in translating external stimuli into neuronal activity and pain (Basbaum et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: Heat-induced pain in mice depends on a trio of heat-activated TRP channels: TRPM3, TRPA1, and TRPV1.
source: For instance, we recently demonstrated that heat-induced pain in mice depends on a trio of heat-activated TRP channels, TRPM3, TRPA1, and TRPV1 (Vandewauw et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Robust neuronal and behavioral heat responses were observed as long as at least one of the three TRP channels (TRPM3, TRPA1, TRPV1) was functional.
source: Robust neuronal and behavioral heat responses were observed as long as at least one of these three TRP channels was functional, but were fully abolished in Trpm3-/-/Trpv1-/-/Trpa1-/- triple knockout mice (Vandewauw et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Heat responses were fully abolished in Trpm3-/-/Trpv1-/-/Trpa1-/- triple knockout mice.
source: Robust neuronal and behavioral heat responses were observed as long as at least one of these three TRP channels was functional, but were fully abolished in Trpm3-/-/Trpv1-/-/Trpa1-/- triple knockout mice (Vandewauw et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: There is triple redundancy of the molecular sensors for acute heat.
source: These results indicate triple redundancy of the molecular sensors for acute heat.
evidence: This claim is an inference from the cited experimental results showing that any one of the three channels is sufficient for heat responses.

claim: There is no redundancy for the development of heat hypersensitivity in inflammatory conditions.
source: Intriguingly, however, there apparently is no such redundancy for the development of heat hypersensitivity in inflammatory conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from cited literature showing that ablation of either TRPV1 or TRPM3 alone is sufficient to suppress inflammatory heat hyperalgesia.

claim: Genetic ablation or pharmacological inhibition of either only TRPV1 or only TRPM3 is sufficient to fully suppress inflammatory heat hyperalgesia.
source: Indeed, genetic ablation or pharmacological inhibition of either only TRPV1 (Caterina et al., 2000; Davis et al., 2000; Gavva et al., 2005; Honore et al., 2005) or only TRPM3 (Alkhatib et al., 2019; Vriens et al., 2011; Straub et al., 2013) is sufficient to fully suppress inflammatory heat hyperalgesia.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple prior studies.

claim: TRPM3 mRNA levels in ipsilateral, WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons were increased to 163% of the levels in WGA-AF647+ neurons on the contralateral side.
source: On average, TRPM3 mRNA levels in the ipsilateral, WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons were increased to 163% (95% confidence interval [CI], 122% to 222%; p=0.008) of the levels in the WGA-AF647+ neurons on the contralateral side, and to 133% (CI, 108–163%; p=0.005) of the levels in WGA-AF647- neurons on the ipsilateral side.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative RNAscope data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: TRPM3 mRNA levels in ipsilateral, WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons were increased to 133% of the levels in WGA-AF647- neurons on the ipsilateral side.
source: On average, TRPM3 mRNA levels in the ipsilateral, WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons were increased to 163% (95% confidence interval [CI], 122% to 222%; p=0.008) of the levels in the WGA-AF647+ neurons on the contralateral side, and to 133% (CI, 108–163%; p=0.005) of the levels in WGA-AF647- neurons on the ipsilateral side.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative RNAscope data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Almost all (98 ± 2%) of the ipsilateral, WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons showed a positive RNAscope signal for TRPM3.
source: Notably, almost all (98 ± 2%) of the ipsilateral, WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons in the six tested animals showed a positive RNAscope signal for TRPM3, compared to between 70% and 80% TRPM3-positive neurons in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647- and contralateral DRG neurons (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative RNAscope data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Between 70% and 80% of ipsilateral WGA-AF647- and contralateral DRG neurons showed a positive RNAscope signal for TRPM3.
source: Notably, almost all (98 ± 2%) of the ipsilateral, WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons in the six tested animals showed a positive RNAscope signal for TRPM3, compared to between 70% and 80% TRPM3-positive neurons in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647- and contralateral DRG neurons (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative RNAscope data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: No significant inflammation-related changes were observed in mRNA levels of TRPA1 or TRPV1.
source: In contrast, we did not observe significant inflammation-related changes in mRNA levels of TRPA1 or TRPV1 (Figure 1D–G and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative RNAscope data shown in Figures 1D-G.

claim: TRPA1 mRNA levels in ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons amounted to 120% of the level in contralateral WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons.
source: For TRPA1, mRNA levels in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons amounted to 120% (CI, 63% to 147%; p=0.56) of the level in the contralateral WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons and to 83% (CI, 40% to 139%; p=0.81) of the level in ipsilateral WGA-AF647- neurons (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative RNAscope data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: TRPA1 mRNA levels in ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons amounted to 83% of the level in ipsilateral WGA-AF647- neurons.
source: For TRPA1, mRNA levels in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons amounted to 120% (CI, 63% to 147%; p=0.56) of the level in the contralateral WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons and to 83% (CI, 40% to 139%; p=0.81) of the level in ipsilateral WGA-AF647- neurons (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative RNAscope data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: TRPV1 mRNA levels in ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons amounted to 89% of the level in contralateral WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons.
source: In the case of TRPV1, mRNA levels in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons amounted to 89% (CI, 53% to 140%; p=0.52) of the level in the contralateral WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons and to 126% (CI, 87% to 166%; p=0.15) of the level in ipsilateral WGA-AF647- neurons (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative RNAscope data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: TRPV1 mRNA levels in ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons amounted to 126% of the level in ipsilateral WGA-AF647- neurons.
source: In the case of TRPV1, mRNA levels in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons amounted to 89% (CI, 53% to 140%; p=0.52) of the level in the contralateral WGA-AF647+ DRG neurons and to 126% (CI, 87% to 166%; p=0.15) of the level in ipsilateral WGA-AF647- neurons (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative RNAscope data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The fraction of TRPA1- or TRPV1-positive DRG neurons did not differ significantly between WGA-AF647+ and WGA-AF647- DRG neurons on the ipsilateral and contralateral sides.
source: Likewise, the fraction of TRPA1- or TRPV1-positive DRG neurons did not differ significantly between WGA-AF647+ and WGA-AF647-DRG neurons on the ipsilateral and contralateral sides (Figure 1E,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative RNAscope data shown in Figures 1E and 1G.

claim: Inflammation is associated with increased transcription of TRPM3, specifically in sensory neurons innervating the inflamed tissue.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that inflammation is associated with an increased transcription of TRPM3, specifically in sensory neurons innervating the inflamed tissue, whereas no inflammation-related changes were found in the mRNA levels of TRPV1 and TRPA1.
evidence: This claim is an inference from the RNAscope data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Procedures to isolate and culture DRG neurons significantly alter the expression levels of many ion channels.
source: Since procedures to isolate and culture DRG neurons significantly alter the expression levels of many ion channels (Wangzhou et al., 2020), we developed an assay where the DRG was imaged as a whole in situ, using spinning-disk confocal imaging (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: TRPV1-lineage neurons include all DRG neurons involved in thermosensation and inflammatory thermal hyperalgesia.
source: For these experiments, we made use of a mouse line that expresses the genetically encoded calcium sensor GCaMP3 in TRPV1-lineage neurons (TRPV1-GCaMP3 mice), which include all the neurons involved in thermosensation and inflammatory thermal hyperalgesia (Mishra and Hoon, 2010; Mishra et al., 2011; Usoskin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Not all GCaMP3-positive DRG neurons from TRPV1-GCaMP3 mice functionally express TRPV1 at the developmental stage analyzed.
source: It is important to note that not all GCaMP3-positive DRG neurons from TRPV1-GCaMP3 mice functionally express TRPV1 at the developmental stage where we did our analysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: TRPV1-lineage neurons identified based on GCaMP3 fluorescence include all DRG neurons that functionally express TRPV1 and TRPA1, but also a subset of DRG neurons that no longer expressed TRPV1.
source: Indeed, in line with earlier studies (Mishra et al., 2011), we found that TRPV1-lineage neurons identified based on their GCaMP3 fluorescence include all DRG neurons that functionally express TRPV1 and TRPA1, but also a subset of DRG neurons that no longer expressed TRPV1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and citation to prior work.

claim: The efficiency of retrograde labeling was similar in the ipsi- and contralateral side, with 25.8 ± 9.7% and 27.7 ± 5.7% of the neurons being WGA-AF647+, respectively.
source: The efficiency of the retrograde labeling was similar in the ipsi- and contralateral side, with 25.8 ± 9.7% and 27.7 ± 5.7% of the neurons being WGA-AF647+, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the retrograde labeling experiments.

claim: The fraction of ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons that exhibited a positive response to TRPM3 agonists increased significantly to 52% compared to around 20% in the different control groups.
source: Importantly, responses to TRPM3 agonists were strongly increased in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons. The fraction of these neurons that exhibited a positive response increased significantly, to 52% compared to around 20% in the different control groups (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The response amplitude to TRPM3 agonists in ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons was increased to 233% when compared to ipsilateral WGA-AF647- neurons.
source: Likewise, the response amplitude in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons was increased to 233% ([CI], 157% to 330%; p=0.007) when compared to the ipsilateral WGA-AF647- neurons and to 448% ([CI], 265% to 755%; p=7 × 10−7) when compared to the WGA-AF647+ contralateral neurons (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The response amplitude to TRPM3 agonists in ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons was increased to 448% when compared to WGA-AF647+ contralateral neurons.
source: Likewise, the response amplitude in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons was increased to 233% ([CI], 157% to 330%; p=0.007) when compared to the ipsilateral WGA-AF647- neurons and to 448% ([CI], 265% to 755%; p=7 × 10−7) when compared to the WGA-AF647+ contralateral neurons (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: There is a strong functional upregulation of TRPM3, specifically in neurons innervating the inflamed paw.
source: These findings indicate a strong functional upregulation of TRPM3, specifically in neurons innervating the inflamed paw.
evidence: This claim is an inference from the calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The fraction of responding neurons to TRPA1 agonists in ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons was doubled.
source: In the case of TRPA1, we found that the fraction of responding neurons in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons was doubled and the average response amplitude was increased to 229% ([CI], 146% to 355%; p=2 × 10−5) when compared to the WGA-AF647+ contralateral neurons (Figure 2C,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The average response amplitude to TRPA1 agonists was increased to 229% in ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons when compared to WGA-AF647+ contralateral neurons.
source: In the case of TRPA1, we found that the fraction of responding neurons in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons was doubled and the average response amplitude was increased to 229% ([CI], 146% to 355%; p=2 × 10−5) when compared to the WGA-AF647+ contralateral neurons (Figure 2C,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: There were no significant differences in the fraction of responding neurons or the response amplitudes to TRPA1 agonists between WGA-AF647+ and WGA-AF647- neurons on the ipsilateral side.
source: However, there were no significant differences in the fraction of responding neurons or the response amplitudes between WGA-AF647+ and WGA-AF647- neurons on the ipsilateral side, suggesting that increased responsiveness to TRPA1 agonists may not be limited to neurons innervating the hind paw but affects the entire ipsilateral DRG.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figures 2C and 2E.

claim: Increased responsiveness to TRPA1 agonists may not be limited to neurons innervating the hind paw but affects the entire ipsilateral DRG.
source: However, there were no significant differences in the fraction of responding neurons or the response amplitudes between WGA-AF647+ and WGA-AF647- neurons on the ipsilateral side, suggesting that increased responsiveness to TRPA1 agonists may not be limited to neurons innervating the hind paw but affects the entire ipsilateral DRG.
evidence: This claim is an inference from the calcium imaging data shown in Figures 2C and 2E.

claim: The amplitude of TRPV1 responses in ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons was significantly increased to 140% when compared to ipsilateral WGA-AF647- neurons.
source: However, the amplitude in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons was significantly increased, to 140% ([CI], 109% to 173%; p=0.02) when compared to the ipsilateral WGA-AF647- neurons and to 205% ([CI], 152% to 280%; p=3 × 10−4) when compared to the WGA-AF647+ contralateral neurons (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The amplitude of TRPV1 responses in ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons was significantly increased to 205% when compared to WGA-AF647+ contralateral neurons.
source: However, the amplitude in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons was significantly increased, to 140% ([CI], 109% to 173%; p=0.02) when compared to the ipsilateral WGA-AF647- neurons and to 205% ([CI], 152% to 280%; p=3 × 10−4) when compared to the WGA-AF647+ contralateral neurons (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Neurons that innervate the inflamed paw show enhanced responses to agonists of TRPM3, TRPA1, and TRPV1.
source: These findings indicate that the neurons that innervate the inflamed paw show enhanced responses to agonists of TRPM3, TRPA1, and TRPV1.
evidence: This claim is an inference from the calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2.

claim: In ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons, there was a pronounced increase in the fraction of neurons that show functional responses to agonists for both TRPM3 and TRPV1.
source: Notably, in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons, we observed a pronounced increase in the fraction of neurons that show functional responses to agonists for both TRPM3 and TRPV1, as well as in the fraction that respond to all three agonists (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: In ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons, there was a pronounced increase in the fraction of neurons that respond to all three agonists (TRPM3, TRPA1, TRPV1).
source: Notably, in the ipsilateral WGA-AF647+ neurons, we observed a pronounced increase in the fraction of neurons that show functional responses to agonists for both TRPM3 and TRPV1, as well as in the fraction that respond to all three agonists (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Isosakuranetin at 20 µM effectively eliminated the responses to TRPM3 agonists.
source: As expected, isosakuranetin effectively eliminated the responses to TRPM3 agonists, illustrating the suitability of this compound to study TRPM3 functionality in DRG (Figure 2D; Figure 2—figure supplements 2–4).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2D and supplementary figures.

claim: On the contralateral side, isosakuranetin had no significant effect on the responses to MO or capsaicin.
source: On the contralateral side, isosakuranetin had no significant effect on the responses to MO or capsaicin (Figure 2E,F), in line with the reported selectivity of the antagonist for TRPM3 (Krügel et al., 2017; Straub et al., 2013; Jia et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figures 2E and 2F, and citations to prior literature.

claim: Isosakuranetin did not affect the response to the depolarizing high K+ solution.
source: Moreover, isosakuranetin did not affect the response to the depolarizing high K+ solution, indicating that the compound does not Ca2+ via voltage-gated Ca2+ channels.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Isosakuranetin caused a significant inhibition of the response amplitudes to capsaicin and MO on the ipsilateral side.
source: Notably, isosakuranetin caused a significant inhibition of the response amplitudes to capsaicin and MO on the ipsilateral side.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: In the presence of isosakuranetin, there were no longer any significant differences in MO or capsaicin responses between ipsi- and contralateral, WGA-AF647+, and WGA-AF647- neurons.
source: In fact, in the presence of isosakuranetin we no longer detected any significant differences in MO or capsaicin responses between ipsi- and contralateral, WGA-AF647+, and WGA-AF647- neurons (Figure 2E,F; Figure 2—figure supplements 2–4).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figures 2E, 2F, and supplementary figures.

claim: Inflammatory heat hyperalgesia is associated with increased functionality of all three heat-activated TRP channels at the level of the DRG cell bodies.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that inflammatory heat hyperalgesia is associated with the increased functionality of all three heat-activated TRP channels at the level of the DRG cell bodies.
evidence: This claim is an inference from the calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2.

claim: There is a strong enhancement of TRPM3-mediated responses in sensory neurons innervating inflamed tissue.
source: In particular, we report for the first time a strong enhancement of TRPM3-mediated responses, as well as large increase in the fraction of neurons that co-express TRPM3 with TRPV1 and TRPA1.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2.

claim: There is a large increase in the fraction of neurons that co-express TRPM3 with TRPV1 and TRPA1 in inflamed tissue.
source: In particular, we report for the first time a strong enhancement of TRPM3-mediated responses, as well as large increase in the fraction of neurons that co-express TRPM3 with TRPV1 and TRPA1.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of TRPM3 not only suppressed the responses to TRPM3 agonists but also reduced the responses to TRPA1 and TRPV1 agonists in neurons innervating inflamed tissue.
source: Notably, pharmacological inhibition of TRPM3 not only suppressed the responses to TRPM3 agonists but also reduced the responses to TRPA1 and TRPV1 agonists in neurons innervating inflamed tissue.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data with isosakuranetin shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: Increased molecular and functional expression of TRPM3 in the context of tissue inflammation enhances the excitability of sensory neurons.
source: These findings are in line with a model where increased molecular and functional expression of TRPM3 in the context of tissue inflammation enhances the excitability of sensory neurons, which may contribute to augmented responses of these neurons to TRPA1 and TRPV1 agonists.
evidence: This claim is a speculative model proposed to explain the experimental findings.

claim: Enhanced TRPM3 activity may contribute to augmented responses of sensory neurons to TRPA1 and TRPV1 agonists.
source: These findings are in line with a model where increased molecular and functional expression of TRPM3 in the context of tissue inflammation enhances the excitability of sensory neurons, which may contribute to augmented responses of these neurons to TRPA1 and TRPV1 agonists.
evidence: This claim is a speculative model proposed to explain the experimental findings.

claim: The responsive area to TRPM3 agonists was increased to 274% in inflamed skin when compared to the contralateral side.
source: The responsive area was increased to 274% ([CI], 138% to 481%; p=0.04) for TRPM3 agonism, to 197% ([CI], 122% to 281%; p=0.02) for TRPA1 agonism and to 256% ([CI], 156% to 359%; p=0.02) for TRPV1 agonism, when compared to the contralateral side.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data from skin nerve endings shown in Figures 4C-E.

claim: The responsive area to TRPA1 agonists was increased to 197% in inflamed skin when compared to the contralateral side.
source: The responsive area was increased to 274% ([CI], 138% to 481%; p=0.04) for TRPM3 agonism, to 197% ([CI], 122% to 281%; p=0.02) for TRPA1 agonism and to 256% ([CI], 156% to 359%; p=0.02) for TRPV1 agonism, when compared to the contralateral side.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data from skin nerve endings shown in Figures 4C-E.

claim: The responsive area to TRPV1 agonists was increased to 256% in inflamed skin when compared to the contralateral side.
source: The responsive area was increased to 274% ([CI], 138% to 481%; p=0.04) for TRPM3 agonism, to 197% ([CI], 122% to 281%; p=0.02) for TRPA1 agonism and to 256% ([CI], 156% to 359%; p=0.02) for TRPV1 agonism, when compared to the contralateral side.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data from skin nerve endings shown in Figures 4C-E.

claim: There was a pronounced increase in the surface of nerve endings that showed responses to more than one agonist in inflamed skin.
source: Like in the DRG cell bodies, we observed a pronounced increase in the surface of nerve endings that showed responses to more than one agonist (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data from skin nerve endings shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The increase in TRPM3-mediated responses was primarily observed in nerve endings that also responded to TRPV1 and/or TRPA1 agonists.
source: Notably, the increase in TRPM3-mediated responses was primarily observed in nerve endings that also responded to TRPV1 and/or TRPA1 agonists (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data from skin nerve endings shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: This study represents the first direct observation of functional upregulation of all three heat-activated TRP channels in intact nerve endings in inflamed skin.
source: Overall, these qualitative results represent, to our knowledge, the first direct observation of functional upregulation of all three heat-activated TRP channels in intact nerve endings in inflamed skin.
evidence: This claim is supported by the novel calcium imaging data from skin nerve endings shown in Figure 4.

claim: Following pre-incubation with isosakuranetin, responses to TRPM3 agonists were strongly reduced to 12% when compared to the ipsilateral paw skins measured in the absence of isosakuranetin.
source: Under this condition, responses to TRPM3 agonists were strongly reduced to 12% ([CI], 3% to 45%; p=0.01; Mann-Whitney test) when compared to the ipsilateral paw skins measured in the absence of isosakuranetin.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data from skin nerve endings with isosakuranetin treatment shown in Figure 4C.

claim: In isosakuranetin-treated skin preparations, the surface of nerve endings responding to the TRPA1 and TRPV1 agonists were similar in the ipsilateral and contralateral skin.
source: In these isosakuranetin-treated skin preparations, the surface of nerve endings responding to the TRPA1 and TRPV1 agonists were similar in the ipsilateral and contralateral skin (Figure 4C–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data from skin nerve endings with isosakuranetin treatment shown in Figures 4C-F.

claim: Three TRP channels (TRPM3, TRPV1, and TRPA1) act as redundant sensors of acute heat.
source: In recent work, we demonstrated that three TRP channels (TRPM3, TRPV1, and TRPA1) act as redundant sensors of acute heat: neuronal heat responses and heat-induced pain are preserved in mice in which two of these three TRP channels were genetically ablated, but combined elimination of all three channels fully abolishes the withdrawal reflex from a noxious heat stimulus (Vandewauw et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Neuronal heat responses and heat-induced pain are preserved in mice in which two of the three TRP channels (TRPM3, TRPV1, TRPA1) were genetically ablated.
source: In recent work, we demonstrated that three TRP channels (TRPM3, TRPV1, and TRPA1) act as redundant sensors of acute heat: neuronal heat responses and heat-induced pain are preserved in mice in which two of these three TRP channels were genetically ablated, but combined elimination of all three channels fully abolishes the withdrawal reflex from a noxious heat stimulus (Vandewauw et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Combined elimination of all three TRP channels (TRPM3, TRPV1, TRPA1) fully abolishes the withdrawal reflex from a noxious heat stimulus.
source: In recent work, we demonstrated that three TRP channels (TRPM3, TRPV1, and TRPA1) act as redundant sensors of acute heat: neuronal heat responses and heat-induced pain are preserved in mice in which two of these three TRP channels were genetically ablated, but combined elimination of all three channels fully abolishes the withdrawal reflex from a noxious heat stimulus (Vandewauw et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: There is an absolute requirement of both TRPV1 and TRPM3 for the development of inflammatory heat hypersensitivity.
source: Notably, earlier work had also revealed an absolute requirement of both TRPV1 and TRPM3 for the development of inflammatory heat hypersensitivity, since genetic ablation or pharmacological inhibition of either channel individually fully abrogates heat hyperalgesia in the rodent CFA model (Caterina et al., 2000; Davis et al., 2000; Gavva et al., 2005; Honore et al., 2005; Alkhatib et al., 2019; Krügel et al., 2017; Vriens et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple prior studies.

claim: Genetic ablation or pharmacological inhibition of either TRPV1 or TRPM3 individually fully abrogates heat hyperalgesia in the rodent CFA model.
source: Notably, earlier work had also revealed an absolute requirement of both TRPV1 and TRPM3 for the development of inflammatory heat hypersensitivity, since genetic ablation or pharmacological inhibition of either channel individually fully abrogates heat hyperalgesia in the rodent CFA model (Caterina et al., 2000; Davis et al., 2000; Gavva et al., 2005; Honore et al., 2005; Alkhatib et al., 2019; Krügel et al., 2017; Vriens et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple prior studies.

claim: Inflammation modulates the functional interplay between heat-activated TRP channels leading to pathological heat hypersensitivity.
source: These combined findings suggested that inflammation modulates the functional interplay between these heat-activated TRP channels leading to pathological heat hypersensitivity, but the underlying processes and mechanisms remained unclear.
evidence: This claim is an inference from the cited literature showing differential requirements for acute heat sensing versus inflammatory hyperalgesia.

claim: Acute inflammation is associated with an increased TRPM3 expression at the mRNA level, specifically in DRG neurons innervating the inflamed paw.
source: Here, by directly comparing the levels of mRNA expression and functional activity of TRPM3, TRPV1 and TRPA1 between sensory neurons innervating the healthy and inflamed hind paw in mice, we arrive at the following novel conclusions: (1) acute inflammation is associated with an increased TRPM3 expression at the mRNA level, specifically in DRG neurons innervating the inflamed paw; no significant changes were detected in the mRNA levels for TRPA1 or TRPV1;
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope data shown in Figure 1.

claim: No significant changes were detected in the mRNA levels for TRPA1 or TRPV1 in DRG neurons innervating the inflamed paw.
source: Here, by directly comparing the levels of mRNA expression and functional activity of TRPM3, TRPV1 and TRPA1 between sensory neurons innervating the healthy and inflamed hind paw in mice, we arrive at the following novel conclusions: (1) acute inflammation is associated with an increased TRPM3 expression at the mRNA level, specifically in DRG neurons innervating the inflamed paw; no significant changes were detected in the mRNA levels for TRPA1 or TRPV1;
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope data shown in Figures 1D-G.

claim: Increased TRP channel functionality is detected both in the neuronal cell bodies and in the nerve endings in the inflamed skin.
source: (2) inflammation is associated with increased functionality of TRPM3, TRPA1 and TRPV1 in DRG neurons, as evidenced by increased Ca2+ responses to specific agonists; this increased functionality is detected both in the neuronal cell bodies and in the nerve endings in the inflamed skin;
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: Increased TRP channel activity in inflammatory conditions is associated with an increase in the fraction of cell bodies and nerve endings that functionally co-express TRPM3 with TRPV1 and TRPA1.

evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4 and Figure 4F.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of TRPM3 not only eliminates Ca2+ responses to TRPM3 agonists, but also reduces responses to TRPV1 and TRPA1 agonists in neurons innervating the inflamed paw.
source: (4) pharmacological inhibition of TRPM3 not only eliminates Ca2+ responses to TRPM3 agonists, but also reduces responses to TRPV1 and TRPA1 agonists in neurons innervating the inflamed paw.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data with isosakuranetin shown in Figures 2E, 2F, and 4C-E.

claim: This is the first study pointing at possible inflammation-induced alterations in TRPM3 expression at the mRNA level.
source: Whereas this is, to our knowledge, the first study pointing at possible inflammation-induced alterations in TRPM3 expression at the mRNA level, earlier studies had already investigated alterations in TRPA1 and TRPV1 mRNA using the rodent CFA model.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' knowledge of the literature and their novel findings.

claim: Several earlier studies report that transcript levels for TRPV1 were found unchanged after CFA treatment when assessed using quantitative PCR or RNA protection assays.
source: In line with our current results, several earlier studies report that transcript levels for TRPV1 were found unchanged after CFA treatment when assessed using quantitative PCR or RNA protection assays (Endres-Becker et al., 2007; Ji et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Some earlier studies found increased levels of TRPA1 mRNA in lumbar DRG following CFA treatment of the hind paw.
source: However, some earlier studies found increased levels of TRPA1 mRNA in lumbar DRG following CFA treatment of the hind paw (Obata et al., 2005; Zhou et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In earlier studies that found increased TRPA1 mRNA, bulk mRNA from entire ganglia was analyzed, which inevitably includes not only neurons that innervate injured tissue, but also neurons from the same DRG that innervate healthy tissue, as well as non-neuronal cells.
source: It should be noted, however, that in these earlier studies, bulk mRNA from entire ganglia was analyzed, which inevitably includes not only neurons that innervate injured tissue, but also neurons from the same DRG that innervate healthy tissue, as well as non-neuronal cells present in DRG such as satellite glia (Shin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is based on knowledge of the methods used in prior studies and citation to literature on DRG composition.

claim: The approach using quantitative in situ hybridization and retrograde labeling allowed specific measurement of mRNA levels in the cell bodies of sensory neurons that innervate the inflamed or control hind paw.
source: In contrast, our approach using quantitative in situ hybridization and retrograde labeling allowed us to specifically measure mRNA levels in the cell bodies of the sensory neurons that innervate the inflamed or control hind paw.
evidence: This claim describes the novel methodological approach used in this study.

claim: An overall increase in TRPA1 mRNA in the order of 30% or less would not be revealed in the statistical analysis due to significant variability in TRPA1 mRNA levels between individual DRG neurons.
source: On the other hand, given the significant variability in TRPA1 mRNA levels between individual DRG neurons observed in our RNA-scope experiments, and the relatively limited number of neurons that were identified as WGA-AF647+, we consider the possibility that an overall increase in TRPA1 mRNA in the order of 30% or less would not be revealed in our statistical analysis.
evidence: This claim is a speculation about potential limitations of the study.

claim: The acute ex vivo preparation of the spinal column avoids the potential loss of specific neuronal populations and rapid alterations in their functional properties that are inherent to the isolation and culturing of DRG neurons.
source: First, we developed an acute ex vivo preparation of the relevant part of the spinal column, where the cell bodies of sensory neurons were imaged within an intact DRG, but lacking the peripheral input. This preparation avoids the potential loss of specific neuronal populations as well as rapid alterations in their functional properties that are inherent to the isolation and culturing of DRG neurons (Wangzhou et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to literature on the effects of DRG neuron isolation and describes the advantage of the novel method.

claim: Increased activity of TRPV1 and TRPA1 in DRG neurons following CFA-induced inflammation is fully in line with earlier work.
source: Increased activity of TRPV1 and TRPA1 in DRG neurons following CFA-induced inflammation is fully in line with earlier work (Zhou et al., 2013; Breese et al., 2005; Nicholas et al., 1999), but this study is, to our knowledge, the first to reveal the specific increase in the subpopulation of DRG co-expressing the three heat-sensing TRP channels.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: This study is the first to reveal the specific increase in the subpopulation of DRG neurons co-expressing the three heat-sensing TRP channels following inflammation.
source: Increased activity of TRPV1 and TRPA1 in DRG neurons following CFA-induced inflammation is fully in line with earlier work (Zhou et al., 2013; Breese et al., 2005; Nicholas et al., 1999), but this study is, to our knowledge, the first to reveal the specific increase in the subpopulation of DRG co-expressing the three heat-sensing TRP channels.
evidence: This claim is based on the novel findings shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The skin preparation used is identical to the saphenous skin–nerve preparation that has been widely studied using extracellular electrodes to measure propagated action potentials from the receptive fields of single sensory nerve endings in the skin.
source: The skin preparation that we used is identical to the saphenous skin–nerve preparation that has been widely studied using extracellular electrodes to measure propagated action potentials from the receptive fields of single sensory nerve endings in the skin, including responses evoked by TRP channel agonists such as capsaicin (Reeh, 1986; Zimmermann et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature describing the skin-nerve preparation.

claim: The novel imaging approach allowed demonstration for the first time that TRPM3, TRPA1, and TRPV1 show a pattern of partial spatial functional overlap in peripheral nerve endings in the skin.
source: This novel imaging approach allowed us to demonstrate for the first time that TRPM3, TRPA1, and TRPV1 show a pattern of partial spatial functional overlap in peripheral nerve endings in the skin.
evidence: This claim is supported by the novel calcium imaging data from skin nerve endings shown in Figure 3 and Figure 4.

claim: Results suggest an increase in the surface of nerve endings that functionally express TRPM3 in the skin of the inflamed paw, particularly in endings that also respond to TRPV1 and TRPA1 agonists.
source: Moreover, similar to the findings in the neuronal cell bodies, our results suggest an increase in the surface of nerve endings that functionally express TRPM3 in the skin of the inflamed paw, particularly in endings that also respond to TRPV1 and TRPA1 agonists.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data from skin nerve endings shown in Figure 4.

claim: Isosakuranetin does not inhibit heterologously expressed TRPV1 or TRPA1.
source: Likewise, earlier studies have shown that isosakuranetin does not inhibit heterologously expressed TRPV1 or TRPA1 (Straub et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Increased molecular and functional expression of TRPM3 in neurons innervating inflamed tissue increases the excitability of nociceptors co-expressing TRPA1 and TRPV1, contributing to the augmented responses to agonist stimulation.
source: Instead, these data raise the possibility that increased molecular and functional expression of TRPM3 in neurons innervating inflamed tissue increases the excitability of nociceptors co-expressing TRPA1 and TRPV1, contributing to the augmented responses to agonist stimulation.
evidence: This claim is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: This interpretation provides a straightforward mechanism for the observation that heat hyperalgesia does not develop in TRPM3-deficient mice and is fully alleviated by TRPM3 antagonists.
source: This interpretation also provides a straightforward mechanism for the observation that heat hyperalgesia does not develop in TRPM3-deficient mice and is fully alleviated by TRPM3 antagonists (Alkhatib et al., 2019; Vriens et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is an inference connecting the current findings to prior observations in the literature.

claim: Heat hyperalgesia is strongly attenuated by pharmacological inhibition or genetic ablation of TRPV1.
source: Since heat hyperalgesia is also strongly attenuated by pharmacological inhibition or genetic ablation of TRPV1 (Caterina et al., 2000; Davis et al., 2000; Gavva et al., 2005; Honore et al., 2005), we hypothesize that those DRG neurons that gain functional co-expression of TRPM3 and TRPV1 under inflammatory conditions play a central role in the development of heat hypersensitivity.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: DRG neurons that gain functional co-expression of TRPM3 and TRPV1 under inflammatory conditions play a central role in the development of heat hypersensitivity.
source: Since heat hyperalgesia is also strongly attenuated by pharmacological inhibition or genetic ablation of TRPV1 (Caterina et al., 2000; Davis et al., 2000; Gavva et al., 2005; Honore et al., 2005), we hypothesize that those DRG neurons that gain functional co-expression of TRPM3 and TRPV1 under inflammatory conditions play a central role in the development of heat hypersensitivity.
evidence: This claim is a hypothesis based on the current findings and prior literature.

claim: The present findings provide the first evidence that TRPM3 expression and activity are increased in sensory neurons that innervate acutely inflamed tissue.
source: In conclusion, the present findings provide the first evidence that TRPM3 expression and activity are increased in sensory neurons that innervate acutely inflamed tissue.
evidence: This claim summarizes the novel findings of the study.

claim: There was a marked increase in sensory neurons that functionally co-express TRPM3 with TRPV1 and TRPA1, observed both in the peripheral nerve endings and in the DRG cell bodies.
source: In particular, we found a marked increase in sensory neurons that functionally co-express TRPM3 with TRPV1 and TRPA1, two other TRP channels implicated in heat sensing and inflammatory pain, and this was observed both in the peripheral nerve endings and in the DRG cell bodies.
evidence: This claim summarizes the findings shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4 and Figure 4F.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of TRPM3 reduced TRPV1- and TRPA1-mediated responses in nociceptors innervating the inflamed paw but not in the contralateral control neurons.
source: Strikingly, pharmacological inhibition of TRPM3 also reduced TRPV1- and TRPA1-mediated responses in nociceptors innervating the inflamed paw but not in the contralateral control neurons, suggesting that enhanced TRPM3 activity may contribute to neuronal hyperexcitability under inflammatory conditions.
evidence: This claim summarizes the findings with isosakuranetin shown in Figures 2E, 2F, and 4C-E.

claim: Enhanced TRPM3 activity may contribute to neuronal hyperexcitability under inflammatory conditions.
source: Strikingly, pharmacological inhibition of TRPM3 also reduced TRPV1- and TRPA1-mediated responses in nociceptors innervating the inflamed paw but not in the contralateral control neurons, suggesting that enhanced TRPM3 activity may contribute to neuronal hyperexcitability under inflammatory conditions.
evidence: This claim is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: These results provide a straightforward rationale for the development of TRPM3 antagonists to prevent or alleviate inflammatory pain.
source: Therefore, these results provide a straightforward rationale for the development of TRPM3 antagonists to prevent or alleviate inflammatory pain.
evidence: This claim is an inference about the therapeutic implications of the findings.

claim: Sensory neurons innervating the hind paws of mice have their cell bodies in the dorsal root ganglia, primarily at the lumbar levels L3-L6.
source: Sensory neurons innervating the hind paws of mice have their cell bodies in the dorsal root ganglia, primarily at the lumbar levels L3-L6.
evidence: This claim is based on established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Intraplantar injection of WGA-AF647 resulted in effective labeling of cell bodies of sensory neurons that innervate the injected territory.
source: Therefore, we injected the retrograde label WGA-AF647 intraplantar in both hind paws seven days prior to tissue isolation, which resulted in effective labeling of cell bodies of sensory neurons that innervate the injected territory (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Unilateral inflammation of the hind paw was induced by injecting CFA into the plantar surface 24 hr before tissue collection.
source: We induced an inflammatory response in the ipsilateral hindpaw by injecting CFA into the plantar surface 24 hr before tissue collection; at the same time, the contralateral hindpaw was injected with vehicle (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental procedure shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Single-molecule fluorescent RNA in situ hybridization (RNAscope) was used to quantify the levels of mRNA encoding TRPM3, TRPA1 and TRPV1 in the ipsi- and contralateral DRGs.
source: We used single-molecule fluorescent RNA in situ hybridization (RNAscope) (Wang et al., 2014), to quantify the levels of mRNA encoding TRPM3, TRPA1 and TRPV1 in the ipsi- and contralateral DRGs (Figure 1A), and compared the levels of mRNA, both between retrogradely labeled (WGA-AF647+) and unlabeled (WGA-AF647-) neurons on the ipsilateral side, and between WGA-AF647+ neurons on the ipsi- versus contralateral side.
evidence: This claim describes the experimental method used, supported by citation to the RNAscope method.
